phases.name: Baseline
phases.note: Work up to a set of 5 with 2 reps left on each main lift; train at about 90% of it.

back_squat.name: Back squat

oldBest.note: Cameron, Nov 24 2026: 'Ive backsquated up to 245', a single ('I could probaly go higher with dedicated effort').

standard.label: Intermediate at 165 lb
standard.note: Strength Level community standards, men, 1RM (strengthlevel.com, read Nov 24 2026): Intermediate = stronger than 50% of lifters who log the lift. Between the 160 lb row (265) and the 170 lb row (282). Novice 206, Advanced 350.

back_squat.cue: Regular back squat. Build depth over the first two weeks before adding weight. Knee sharp? Squat to a box with a 3-s lowering instead.
tips: Big breath and brace before every rep.
Control the way down, drive up fast.

rdl.name: Romanian deadlift
rdl.slow: 3 s down to the hamstring stretch, no bounce
tips: Push the hips back until the hamstrings stretch.
Bar stays against the legs; back flat.

calf_raise.name: Standing calf raise
calf_raise.slow: 2 s down, 2 s pause at the bottom
calf_raise.keepTempo: Pause 2 seconds at the bottom of every rep.
tips: Full stretch and a 2-second pause at the bottom.
No bouncing.

bss.name: Bulgarian split squat
bss.slow: 3 s down, knee tracking over the toes
bss.cue: Tuck the pelvis on the back leg.
tips: Slow down, front foot flat, knee tracks over toes.
Lean slightly forward and drive through the front heel.

leg_curl.name: Seated leg curl
leg_curl.slow: 3 s letting the pad back up
tips: Squeeze hard at the bottom of the curl.
Take 3 seconds letting the pad back up.

curl.name: Standing dumbbell curl
tips: Elbows pinned to your sides; no swing.
Lower all the way to straight arms.

oh_tri_ext.name: Overhead triceps extension
oh_tri_ext.slow: 3 s down into the stretch, 1 s pause
tips: Let the weight sink for a deep stretch behind the head.
Elbows point up and stay in.

ab_wheel.name: Ab wheel
ab_wheel.slow: 3 s out, 2 s back, hips never sag
tips: Ribs down, glutes tight; hips must not sag.
Only roll out as far as you can hold that shape.

strict_press.name: Strict press
tips: Squeeze glutes and abs; no lean back.
Bar travels straight up, head through at the top.

weighted_pullup.name: Weighted pull-up

standard.label: Intermediate, all men
standard.note: Strength Level community standards, men, 1RM (strengthlevel.com, read Nov 24 2026): Intermediate = stronger than 50% of lifters who log the lift. Added weight, all bodyweights. Novice +29, Advanced +114.

weighted_pullup.cue: 30-45 s dead hang after the last set.
tips: Start every rep from a dead hang.
Chest to the bar, then lower under control.

incline_db_press.name: Incline dumbbell press
tips: Lower until you feel the upper chest stretch, pause, press.
Shoulder blades pinned back and down; a steeper bench turns this into a shoulder press.

cs_row.name: Chest-supported row
tips: Pull the elbows back and squeeze for a second.
Chest stays on the pad; let the shoulders reach forward at the bottom.

lateral_raise.name: Lateral raise
tips: Lead with the elbows, raise out and slightly forward.
Lower slowly; no shrugging or swinging.

incline_curl.name: Incline dumbbell curl
incline_curl.slow: 3 s down, pause with straight arms
tips: Arms hang straight down behind the body; feel the stretch.
Shoulders stay back on the bench.

t2b.name: Toes-to-bar
tips: Start each rep by pressing down on the bar with straight arms.
Control the swing down; no wild kip.

face_pull.name: Face pull
tips: Pull to eye level, hands apart, thumbs back.
Hold the squeeze for a second.

power_clean.name: Power clean
power_clean.cue: Fast. Hang power clean if the catch bothers the knee.
tips: Patient off the floor, then jump hard.
Fast elbows; reset fully between reps.

front_squat.name: Front squat

standard.label: Intermediate at 165 lb
standard.note: Strength Level community standards, men, 1RM (strengthlevel.com, read Nov 24 2026): Intermediate = stronger than 50% of lifters who log the lift. Between the 160 lb row (210) and the 170 lb row (222). Novice 164, Advanced 277.

tips: Elbows high the whole rep.
Sit straight down, chest tall, drive up fast.

push_press.name: Push press

standard.label: Intermediate, all men
standard.note: Strength Level community standards, men, 1RM (strengthlevel.com, read Nov 24 2026): Intermediate = stronger than 50% of lifters who log the lift. All bodyweights; the site does not split the push press by bodyweight. Novice 129, Advanced 240.

tips: Short, straight dip with heels down.
Drive hard with the legs, then punch to lockout.

db_row.name: Dumbbell row
tips: Pull the elbow toward the hip, not straight up.
Full stretch at the bottom; no torso twist.

preacher_curl.name: Dumbbell preacher curl
tips: Lower to nearly straight and pause in the stretch.
Upper arm stays glued to the pad.

rope_pushdown.name: Rope pushdown
tips: Elbows stay at your sides.
Spread the rope and squeeze at the bottom.

side_plank.name: Side plank
side_plank.cue: Pelvis tucked. Copenhagen plank once this is easy.
tips: Straight line from head to heels, hips pushed forward.

items.name: Couch stretch
items.cue: Tuck pelvis, squeeze back glute, pad the knee. Swap to half-kneeling or side-lying quad stretch if the kneecap hurts.

sessions.name: Lift 1: Legs
sessions.goal: Leg strength and size. The squat is the priority: hit your reps with 2-3 left in the tank. Then hamstrings, calves and single-leg work, with arms and abs to finish.

sessions.name: Lift 2: Upper

blocks.name: Engine
blocks.cue: RPE 8: finish each minute with 10-20 s to spare. Rest is what's left of the minute.

stations.name: Echo bike, 12-15 cal
stations.cue: Arms and legs together, hard from the first second.

alt.name: Row, 15-18 cal
alt.cue: Concept2, damper 4-5. Legs, then body, then arms. Echo bike instead if the knee complains.

stations.name: Kettlebell swings x 12
stations.cue: A heavy bell you can snap for 12 (one of the black ones). Snap the hips; the arms just guide the bell.

stations.name: Leg raises x 6-10 + 5 slam balls
stations.cue: Leg raises on the captain's chair (the dip station), no swing. Then 5 slams with the 20 lb slam ball. Push-ups instead of slams if the back complains.

alt.name: Sled push, 2 lengths
alt.cue: Load the sled before the Engine starts: heavy enough that you have to drive, light enough to keep moving. No lowering and no landing, so it is easy on the knee.

test.name: 2,000 m row test
test.cue: Benchmark on the Concept2, damper 4-5. Steady first 500 m, then build; the last 500 m all out. Tap Next when you finish and note your time. Knee complaining? 10 min on the Echo bike for max calories instead, and retest the same way.

test.name: 2,000 m row retest
test.cue: Beat your week 2 time, same damper. Tap Next when you finish and note your time.

blocks.note: Replaces the old toes-to-bar, calf raise and face pull block (v1.11). Calf raises moved to the Friday finisher. v1.21.0 (Cameron, Nov 25: no ski erg in the functional room; it has a Rogue Echo bike, a Concept2 rower, a push sled, kettlebells, slam balls and a captain's chair): the ski erg is out. Minute 1 is the Echo bike, the rower in weeks 4, 6, 8 and 10 (a station's alt takes its place in those weeks); minute 3 is leg raises and slam balls, a sled push in the rower weeks. The week 2 and 12 benchmark is a 2,000 m row.

sessions.goal: Upper-body strength. Press and weighted pull-up are the priority, then chest and back, then arm and shoulder size work taken close to failure.

sessions.name: Lift 3: Full body

items.name: Empty-bar clean + front squat complex x2

sessions.goal: Full-body power and strength. Fast, crisp cleans first, then front squat and push press, with arms and core to finish.

runs.name: Run 1: Intervals
runs.note: Warm up with 5 min easy jogging. Then rounds of fast and easy: weeks 1-4, 5 x 2 min fast / 2 min easy; weeks 5-8, 5 x 3 / 2; weeks 9-12, 4 x 4 / 2-3. Run the fast parts by pace. Until your first 5K check-in: 7:45-8:15 per mile for 2 min, 8:00-8:25 for 3 min, 8:10-8:35 for 4 min. After it, the paces come from your latest 5K (Daniels' interval pace), so they get faster as you do. Heart rate is the check: it should reach 170-180 by the end of each fast part, 90-95% of a 31-year-old's max of about 189 (it lags, so it is still climbing in the first minute). Over 180 before the end means ease off a little. Easy is a jog or a walk until heart rate is under 160. Cool down with 3 min easy, then the stretch block. Weeks 3, 7 and 12: a 5K check-in instead, about every 4-5 weeks, measured against a fit 31-year-old's 23:00.
runs.effort: fast by pace, heart rate as the check

tests.name: 5K check-in
lines: Warm up: 10 min easy, with 4 short pickups of about 20 s.
Run: 5K (3.1 mi) as fast as you can hold evenly. Start a little slower than you think; the last mile is all out.
After: 5 min easy, then the stretch block.
Count it as the 5K test. The app reads your fastest 5K from the watch and sets your interval paces from it.
tests.why: First benchmark: the interval paces come from it (Nov 26 run plan review).

tests.name: 5K check-in
lines: Warm up: 10 min easy, with 4 short pickups of about 20 s.
Run: 5K (3.1 mi) as fast as you can hold evenly. Start a little slower than you think; the last mile is all out.
After: 5 min easy, then the stretch block.
Count it as the 5K test. Your interval paces move with your time.
tests.why: The lighter week: fresher legs for the test, and it stands in for that week's intervals.

tests.name: 5K check-in
lines: Warm up: 10 min easy, with 4 short pickups of about 20 s.
Run: 5K (3.1 mi) as fast as you can hold evenly. Start a little slower than you think; the last mile is all out.
After: 5 min easy, then the stretch block.
Count it as the 5K test. Compare it with your week 3 time.
tests.why: Retest week for the whole block.

runs.testsWhy: Every 4-5 weeks (Cameron, Nov 26: regular 5K check-ins that update the plan). McMillan: recalculate training paces about every 4-8 weeks. VDOT O2 (Daniels): update paces from a recent race or time trial, otherwise about 1 VDOT point every 4-6 weeks. A 5K time trial varies about 1% test to test (Sunderland parkrun study: typical error 14.7 s, CV 0.95%), so 2 weeks of gains would hide in the noise; 4-5 weeks of interval training should show 2-4%.

paceFrom5k.why: Daniels' interval pace, 97-100% of the VDOT the 5K gives (Daniels & Gilbert equations); for a 23:00 runner that is 7:04-7:15, the same as 3K race pace (7:10) and McMillan's 15-minute race pace (7:14). Shorter reps a little faster, longer a little slower, to the nearest 5 s.

fiveKCheck.why: A 5K outside 14:00-45:00, or more than 5% off the last good one, waits for Cameron's OK before it moves the paces (his Nov 19 rule on numbers that look wrong). Test-to-test noise is about 1%; 4-5 weeks of training rarely moves a 5K more than 2-4%.

goal.why: Fit 31-year-old man: USATF 2025 age grading at age 30 (60% = 21:22, 50% = 25:38), Daniels' levels (Novice 24:00, Intermediate 20:00), US race data (top 10% of men about 22:06).

hr.why: Nov 26 2026, Cameron: base it on a fit runner his age, at least 3 sources. Max heart rate about 189 at 31 (Fox 220-age 189, Tanaka 2001 186, HUNT/Nes 2013 191). Fast parts end at 90-95% of it (Helgerud 2007 4x4; Stöggl & Sperlich 2015, top zone over 90%; Daniels' interval zone near max).

runs.name: Run 2: Long easy run
runs.note: Easy: heart rate 130-150, a pace where you can talk in full sentences (a fit 31-year-old runs about 9:00-9:45 per mile there; go by heart rate, not pace). If heart rate passes 150, slow down or walk a minute. Start 3.5 mi, then add 0.5 mi each time, but never more than 10% past your longest run in the last 30 days, up to 6-7 mi. A ski day replaces it, but only runs count toward the distance, so after weeks without running it comes back down.
runs.effort: Heart rate 130-150, easy enough to talk

distance.why: Frandsen et al., Br J Sports Med 2025 (5,205 runners on Garmin): a single run 10-30% longer than the longest run in the previous 30 days raised injury risk 64%, over 100% longer more than doubled it. Nov 26 run plan review.

hr.why: Nov 26 2026, Cameron: base it on a fit runner his age, at least 3 sources. Easy tops out at about 79% of a max of 189 (Daniels' easy zone 65-79%; RunnersConnect under about 75%; Powers & Howley zone 1 60-71%).
